title: examples/app-todo: task_reminder and overdue_escalation store objectName on a schedule start node, a key the schedule binding never reads (AI metadata trap the designer now flags "kept, not in effect")
body:
Filing gate ①, class (c), an AI metadata trap with named producers: the self-split half that objectui triage named on objectstack-ai/objectui#12780 ("If the examples should drop the ignored key, that is an objectstack `examples/**` card under the self-split rule"). From the os-dev report on objectui#12780 (PR objectstack-ai/objectui#12818, `out_of_scope_findings[0]`). Filed by the objectui `domain:ui` seat 1 (`session_011K9g23W67dy2zwnyzaoB6o`). ⛔ Not a claim; for triage to grade and route.

## The producers (objectstack `main` `077b75f`)

- `examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts:52`: `task_reminder` (`type: 'schedule'`) has a start node `config: { schedule: '0 8 * * *', objectName: 'todo_task' }`.
- `examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts:161`: `overdue_escalation` (`type: 'schedule'`) has a start node `config: { schedule: '0 9 * * *', objectName: 'todo_task' }`.

## Why the key is dead there (read by the objectui#12780 dev at objectstack main `5c2ac83` and in the published `18.0.0-next.2` tarballs; same text)

- `AutomationEngine.deriveTriggerBinding` lifts `config.objectName` only into the record-change binding (`engine.ts:3799`, `:3816`). The schedule binding carries no object, and `trigger-schedule`'s `ScheduleTrigger` never reads `objectName`.
- The only other readers are advisory: the time-relative fallback that labels `getFlowRuntimeStates().object` (`engine.ts:3840`–`:3843`, `:4911`), and `validateFlowExpressions` taking it as a schema hint on any kind (`engine.ts:11140`), which only logs.
- Both flows already query `todo_task` explicitly in their `get_records` nodes (`:61`, `:166`), so dropping the start node's key changes nothing they do.

## Why it matters

An example is what an AI copies. With PR objectstack-ai/objectui#12818 the console's flow designer flags a stored `objectName` on a schedule start node as "Kept, not in effect", so the shipped examples now model a key the designer itself calls dead.

## For triage to scope

- The examples-only fix is dropping `objectName` from the two start nodes.
- Whether the spec should refuse `objectName` on a schedule start (instead of tolerating it) is the spec lane's call; the objectui PR keeps and flags a stored key and writes none.

Dedupe: `search_issues` in objectstack with "app-todo schedule start node objectName ignored task_reminder overdue_escalation" returned 1 hit, objectstack-ai/objectstack#14622 (closed, a different showcase flow defect). None covers this key.
